title: Protesters clash with police in Paris and across France over living costs and schools
seoTitle: Paris nationwide protests over costs and schools

tea.why: Protesters demonstrate against the high cost of living, soaring prices, and inadequate school funding.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand better school funding, improved wages, and pensions.
tea.changed: Oct 28: Authorities reported nationwide arrests exceeding 1,200 alongside urban clashes and property damage.

summary: Massive protests and marches took place in Paris and across France, drawing hundreds of thousands of participants over living costs and school funding. The movement, which originated from high school staff shortages, expanded nationwide with participation from students and workers. While many demonstrations began peacefully, clashes erupted near endpoints in Paris and other cities such as Marseille, Lyon, and Bordeaux, where some individuals threw projectiles, fireworks, and set street fires. Police responded with tear gas, water cannons, and sound grenades. The Interior Ministry and the CGT union reported contrasting crowd figures, and authorities deployed tens of thousands of security personnel. President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, attributing it to extremist groups and criminals, while trade groups reported severe economic losses and widespread damage to commercial stores.
response: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez deployed up to 70,000 officers backed by water cannons and armored vehicles. Police used tear gas, water cannons, and sound grenades to disperse crowds. President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence and vowed that offenders would be punished.

crowd.text: The Interior Ministry put nationwide turnout at 410,000, while the CGT union estimated nearly 800,000.

arrests.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said police made nearly 1,000 arrests

injuries.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez denounced very serious disturbances during which 60 policemen were injured.

deaths.text: A protester who took to the streets yesterday in Paris against the high cost of living died of cardiac arrest.

updates.text: Clashes erupted in Paris and across French cities as mass marches drew to a close.
The French retail chamber reported severe revenue drops and property damage across inner cities.
Authorities stated that nationwide arrests surpassed 1,200 following widespread urban unrest.
